 This Petition, Coming On For Orders,
This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order
1. Learned HCGP takes notice for the respondent-State.

2. This petition is filed by accused Nos. 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 seeking anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest by respondent - police in Crime No.49/2023 dated 10.04.2023 registered by Kalaburagi City Women Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 324, 355, 504, 506,
307 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

3. The factual matrix of the prosecution case are that, one Smt. Hemalata lodged a complaint before the respondent-police alleging that her marriage was solemnized with accused No.1 Manik Jadhav on 15.04.2022 as per the customs prevailing in their community and in the marriage her parents have given 25 Tolas of gold, cash of Rs.20,000/- and household utensils i.e., A.C., Fridge, Washing Machine, Bed Cot, Sofa Set, TV etc., thereby they have totally spent Rs.37.00 lakhs.
It is further alleged that after the marriage, the complainant and accused No.1 lead happy marital life for about 15 days only.

Thereafter, the accused persons started harassing the complainant by abusing that she is not cooking properly and does not wash clothes properly and they used to abuse her in filthy language and beat her for the reason that her parents given little dowry at the time of marriage and they demanded to bring 10 Tolas of gold and Rs.10,000/- as additional dowry from her parents and gave a threat that otherwise she will be finished.
The parents of the complainant advised the accused persons that they have already given dowry.
It is further alleged in the complaint that the in-laws of the complainant also involved in the alleged harassment to the complainant.

It is the specific case of Lokesh And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27259399/
2 the complainant that on 14.10.2022 the complainant and her husband have shifted to Gubbi Colony,
Kalaburagi, by taking house on rent and they started residing separately, but there also accused No.1 started harassment his wife by consuming alcohol.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accused No.1 told that earlier they have killed by hanging the wife of his brother i.e., petitioner No.1, herein, and to that effect a complaint was already lodged before the Women Police Station, by saying so he threatened the complainant with dire consequence and also assaulted her over her body with an intention to kill her.
He also kicked on her stomach and chest and made an attempt to kill her by pressing her neck.
Hence, the complainant lodged complaint before the respondent-police on 10.04.2023.

Based on the said complaint the respondent-police registered a case against 9 accused persons including the petitioners in Crime No.49/2020, as stated supra.
4.
Aggrieved by the same, petitioners approached the Hon'ble III Additional District and Sessions Judge at Kalaburagi for grant of anticipatory bail in Crl.Misc. No.671/2023.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, the learned Sessions Judge rejected the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail by the order dated 21.04.2023.
Hence, the petitioners are before this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and also learned HCGP for the respondent-State and perused the material available on record.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned HCGP for the respondent,
on a cursory glance of complaint and other available material on record more particularly the investigation papers, it could be seen that except the vague omnibus allegations made against the petitioners in respect of dowry demand, there is no specific allegation in respect of the alleged offence under Section 307 of IPC.
Nevertheless, in the complaint the complainant has made allegations only against her husband i.e., accused No.1 for the alleged assault and attempt to commit her murder.

Moreover it is admitted case of the complainant that from 14.10.2022 herself and her husband i.e., accused No.1 were residing separately at Kalaburagi City in a rented house and thereafter her husband used to harass her both physically and mentally and on 02.11.2022 he assaulted her mercilessly all over her body and made an attempt to commit her murder.
As such, she lodged the complaint.

7. That being the case, since the complainant and her husband were residing separately since one year prior to the date of alleged incident, the allegations against these petitioners has not made out a prima facie case against them for the alleged offences under Sections 498A and 307 of IPC.

The petitioners being the in-laws of the complainant and they are residing separately away from the house of the complainant, in my considered opinion the petitioners may be admitted on anticipatory bail.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., is allowed.

Consequently, the petitioners directed to be released on anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest by respondent-police in connection with Crime No.49/2023 subject to the following conditions.:
